answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with stake-weighted reputation: every agent locks a refundable deposit and earns trust only through paid work peers verify. A new identity starts dim, like an unlit lantern, and must finish many small checkable jobs before its votes or listings carry weight. Honest agents build a steady pulse of completed tasks, while a fake identity echo, identical behavior repeated across many accounts, is easy to detect and slash. Spinning up thousands of sybils then costs thousands of deposits plus weeks of real work, far more than the rewards they could steal.
